2014_067_061714mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of June 17, 2014, held at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Its centerpiece is a public hearing on the proposed 2014-2015 budget presented by Mark Rajter, which sets General Fund revenue at $131,253,100 against expenditures of $132,525,180 and a projected fund balance of $18,040,547 at June 30, 2015. The packet also carries the 2013-14 budget amendment, the 2014-15 appropriations resolution levying 18.0000 non-homestead and 5.2580 homestead operating mills, administrator contract extensions, several bond and food-service bid awards, and May minutes recording the appointment of Dr. Richard Machesky as superintendent.

## Meeting
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, June 17, 2014, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

## Public Hearing: 2014-2015 Proposed Budget (Mark Rajter)
General Fund revenue, 2013-2014 amended budget versus 2014-2015 proposed budget:

| Source | 2013-2014 Amended | 2014-2015 Proposed | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local | 36,487,546 | 36,487,546 | 0 |
| State | 86,197,867 | 83,797,430 | (2,400,437) |
| Federal | 3,346,213 | 3,346,213 | 0 |
| Incoming/Transfers | 7,623,271 | 7,621,911 | (1,360) |
| Total Revenue | $133,654,897 | $131,253,100 | ($2,401,797) |

Expenditures move from Total Instruction of 92,366,286 to 87,742,725 and Total Support Services of 43,864,550 to 44,598,712, with Community Services 145,529 to 147,176 and Outgoing Transfers/Other 36,141 to 36,567. Total Expenditures go from 136,412,506 to 132,525,180; excess revenues over expenditures from (2,757,609) to (1,272,080); beginning fund balance July 1 from 22,070,236 to 19,312,628; ending fund balance June 30 from 19,312,627 to 18,040,548. Revenue is charted at 27.80% Local, 63.84% State, 2.55% Federal and 5.81% Transfers; expenditures at 66.21% Instruction and 33.65% Support Services.

## Budget assumptions
Projected blended student count of 12,590.00, a flat increase from 2013/14; the student-count slide shows a 2014-15 count of 12,539.00 built from Sep 2014 at 11,285.00 (90%) and Feb 2015 at 1,254.00 (10%). Foundation allowance of $8,885.00 per pupil assumes a $50 per pupil increase, plus $50 per pupil for Best Practices and $100 per pupil for performance funding. Retirement rate budgeted with an increase from 29.35% to 30.34% on October 1, 2013, with an effective rate of 25.78% offset by UAAL Rate Stabilization; FICA remains 7.65%. General Fund salary expenditures decreased $1,367,905 from the 2013/14 amended budget, reflecting the absence of the one-time fy 13-14 stipend of $2.4 million and 21 TEA fte retiring. TEA, TESA and TESPA contracts run through June 30, 2015; TESA, TESPA, administrators and non-represented staff receive 0.00% increases, with a 4% off-schedule payment for TESA and TESPA. Millage assumptions: hold harmless 5.2580 mills, non-homestead 18.00 mills, debt 4.70 mills.

| Capital Projects Maintenance | 793,583 | - | - | 793,583 |
| Internal Service | 25,000 | 24,000 | (24,000) | 25,000 |

## Business items
2013-14 budget amendment appropriating General Fund 136,412,506, Special Revenue Funds 8,296,343, Debt Service Funds 12,287,912, Capital Projects Funds 100,000 and Internal Service Fund 25,000. 2014-15 appropriations resolution levying 18.0000 mills non-homestead operating, 11.2580 mills commercial personal property, 5.2580 mills homestead and 4.7000 mills for debt retirement. Bid awards recommended: food service equipment and installation to Stafford-Smith, Inc., $101,968.00; science hardware to Sehi, Inc., $29,550.66; computers to Sehi, Inc., $181,432.82; mobile device management software to CDWG, $208,921.50.

## Personnel and minutes
One-year extensions recommended for Assistant Superintendents Jan Keeling, Mark Rajter and Jasen Witt through June 30, 2016, plus extensions for 34 named administrators. Consent-agenda minutes from May 5, May 6, May 15 and May 20, 2014 record the offer of the superintendency to Dr. Richard Machesky, custodial and food-service contract awards, bond bid approvals, and adoption of revised Board Policies C-1402, G-1005 and J-2012.

PUBLIC HEARING: 2014-2015 PROPOSED BUDGET. Presented by Mark Rajter, with a PowerPoint and a draft 2014-15 budget book marked DRAFT (32 numbered pages). Taxable values charted for 2013-2014 and 2014-2015 are homestead 2,288,017,150 and 2,355,319,780; non-homestead 1,159,504,798 and 1,137,163,050; total taxable value 3,447,521,948 and 3,492,482,830. The foundation grant history chart runs from 7,534 to a final pair of 8,805 and 8,835.

GENERAL FUND SUMMARY. Revenue, 2013-2014 proposed amended budget versus 2014-2015 proposed budget with change: Local 36,487,546 and 36,487,546, change 0; State 86,197,867 and 83,797,430, change (2,400,437); Federal 3,346,213 and 3,346,213, change 0; Incoming 7,623,271 and 7,621,911, change (1,360); Total Revenue $133,654,897 and $131,253,100, change ($2,401,797). The 2014-2015 revenue mix is charted at Local 27.80%, State 63.84%, Federal 2.55% and Transfers 5.81%. Expenditures, same two columns: Basic Programs 75,963,067 and 71,241,541; Added Needs 15,689,339 and 15,785,389; Adult/Cont. Ed. 713,880 and 715,795; Total Instruction 92,366,286 and 87,742,725. Support Service: Pupil 9,547,213 and 9,518,872; Instructional Staff 6,572,182 and 6,625,044; General Administration 2,020,434 and 2,054,420; School Administration 7,752,765 and 8,092,920; Business Services 2,386,077 and 2,432,425; Operation & Maintenance 8,730,239 and 8,918,758; Pupil Transportation 3,397,659 and 3,441,680; Central Services 1,748,927 and 1,789,278; Support Services (Athletics and Other) 1,709,054 and 1,725,315; Total Support Services 43,864,550 and 44,598,712. Community Services 145,529 and 147,176; Outgoing Trans./Other 36,141 and 36,567; Total Expenditures 136,412,506 and 132,525,180; Excess Revenues/(Expend.) (2,757,609) and (1,272,080); Beginning Fund Balance, July 1 22,070,236 and 19,312,628; Ending Fund Balance, June 30 19,312,627 and 18,040,548. Expenditures are charted at Instruction 66.21%, Support Services 33.65%, Community Services 0.11% and Transfers and Other 0.03%. The comparative schedule adds 2012-13 actual Total Revenues 130,643,398 (Local 35,999,921, State 83,529,139, Federal 3,430,090, Interdistrict 7,684,248) and Total Expenditures 131,851,755, with Transfers In 700,012, Transfers Out (500,000), Net Change in Fund Balance (1,008,345) and fund balance moving from 23,078,581 to 22,070,236.

BUDGET ASSUMPTIONS. Projected blended student count of 12,590.00, a flat increase from 2013/14 under the 90% fall / 10% spring formula. Foundation allowance of $8,885.00 per pupil for 2014/15 assuming a $50 per pupil increase, plus $50 per pupil for Best Practices and $100 per pupil for performance funding categorical. Retirement rate budgeted with an increase from 29.35% to 30.34% on October 1, 2013, effective rate 25.78%, offset by UAAL Rate Stabilization; FICA rate 7.65% unchanged; benefits estimated at State-mandated premium caps. Salary expenditures decreased $1,367,905 in the General Fund from the amended 2013/14 budget, attributed to TEA salaries excluding the one-time fy 13-14 stipend of $2.4 million, inclusion of TEA two-step increment costs in fy 14-15, and the salary differential of 21 TEA fte retiring. TEA, TESA and TESPA contracts run through June 30, 2015. The TEA schedule is stretched from 11 to 14 steps with members moving up two steps; TESA and TESPA receive 0.00% salary increases with no step increases plus a 4% off-schedule payment in fy 14-15; administrators 0.00%, with an increase of one administrator in salary and benefits and a reduction of one administrator in contracted staff; non-represented 0.00% with no FTE change. Indirect-cost transfers to the General Fund: Community Education Fund $93,413, Food Service Fund $9,075, Troy Career Center $20,000, Grants $50,578. General Fund expenses exceed revenues by $1,272,080 with projected June 30, 2015 fund balance of $18,040,547. Millage assumptions: hold harmless 5.2580 mills, non-homestead 18.00 mills, debt 4.70 mills. A Capital Project Maintenance Fund established in 2011/12 holds resources for capital infrastructure repairs.

Adult Education Civics $20,000; Adult Education Family Literacy $123,000; IDEA-Flowthrough $1,900,131; IDEA-Preschool $66,656; Michigan School Readiness $161,568; CTE Millage $130,318; Title I $735,518; Title II Part A Teacher/Principal Training $240,304; Title III English Language Acquisition $404,216; and, for the Troy Career Center, Workforce Investment Act $2,783,481 tied to the Oakland County Michigan Works! Service Centers.

The millage history shows 2014-15 homestead totaling 15.9580 (6.0000 State Education Tax, 5.2580 hold harmless, 4.7000 debt), non-homestead 28.7000 (6.0000, 18.0000 statewide, 4.7000 debt), industrial personal property 15.9580 and commercial personal property 21.9580, with a note that in 1993/94 all taxpayers paid 31.0674 mills for operating purposes. A blank Michigan Department of Treasury Form 614 (Rev. 04-14) L-4029 2014 Tax Rate Request, due on or before September 30, 2014 under MCL 211.24e, 211.34 and 211.34d, is included. PERSONNEL. Item 7.B. extends contracts through June 30, 2016 for administrators including Lara Dixon (Principal, Athens High School), Ryan Brinks (International Academy East), Audra Melton (Baker), Joe Duda (Larson), Timothy Fulcher (Smith), Joyce Brasington (Wattles), Janice Brzezinski (Hill), Brian Canfield (Schroeder), Jerry Cottone (Leonard), Tammy DiPonio (Costello), Matt Jansen (Wass), Charles Lesser (Martell), Stephanie Miller (Morse), David Pass (Troy Union), Jeremy Whan (Bemis), assistant principals Melissa Curth, Robert E. Dowd, Bettie A. Goss, James Johnson, Remo Roncone, William Turner, Amy Buchanan, Jonathan Cross, Diane Kocenda and Anthony Morse, plus Michael Jolly (Athletics, CTE and Community Ed), Kerry Birmingham (Community and Media Relations), Kenneth Miller (Maintenance and Operations), Dominick Asaro (Transportation), Sara Konieczka (Human Resources Manager), Anne Mull (Instruction and Assessment), Mark Washington (Technology), Shawna Veit (Special Education) and John Schiesler (Data Processing).

BUSINESS ACTIONS. Item 9.A., the 2013-14 budget amendment, appropriates General Fund $136,412,506, Special Revenue Funds $8,296,343, Debt Service Funds $12,287,912, Capital Projects Funds $100,000 and Internal Service Fund $25,000. General Fund revenues are unchanged at 133,654,897 with fund balance July 1 of 22,070,236 and total available to appropriate of 155,725,133. Expenditure changes include Basic Programs from 72,342,540 to 75,963,067, Added Needs from 16,326,280 to 15,689,339, Total Instruction from 89,382,700 to 92,366,286, Pupil from 9,700,016 to 9,547,213, Instructional Staff from 6,986,977 to 6,572,182, Operations/Maintenance from 8,490,147 to 8,730,239, Community Services from 102,649 to 145,529, Total Support Services from 44,249,248 to 43,864,550 and Total Expenditures from 133,770,738 to 136,412,506, a change of 2,641,768 that moves ending fund balance from 21,954,395 to 19,312,627. Special Revenue local revenue falls from 4,893,006 to 4,711,266 and ending fund balance from 3,113,400 to 2,825,796. Debt Service is unchanged at revenues 16,149,734 and expenditures 12,287,912 with ending balance 923,037. Capital Projects adds 100,000 of other expenditures, moving ending balance to 793,583. Item 9.B., the 2014-15 appropriations resolution, lists General Fund 132,525,180, Special Revenue Funds 7,840,568, Debt Service Funds 16,444,718, Capital Projects/Capital Projects Maintenance Funds $0 and Internal Service Funds 24,000, and levies 18.0000 mills non-homestead general operating, 11.2580 mills commercial personal property, 5.2580 mills homestead and 4.7000 mills on all properties for debt retirement. Item 9.C. awards Bid 9786 food service equipment and installation, replacing the fryers at Athens and Troy High Schools with Unox ChefTop combi ovens, to Stafford-Smith, Inc. for $101,968.00 from the 2013-2014 Food Services Fund; competing totals were Douglas Equipment $96,207.48, Great Lakes Hotel Supply Company $103,956.00 and Gold Star Products $109,798.40, with a 12 June 2014 memorandum from Kenneth D. Miller noting Douglas Equipment bid an unapproved unit. Item 9.D. awards science hardware to Sehi, Inc. for $29,550.66 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, covering 60 HP 340 G1 laptops at $441.12 and 7 HP external USB DVD drives at $54.78, per a June 1, 2014 memo from Mark Washington citing Laura Ritter. Item 9.E. awards computers to Sehi, Inc. for $181,432.82, of which $89,440.80 is charged to the 2013-2014 TRIG grant and $91,992.02 to the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, for 359 HP 800 G-series workstations at $528.48 and $481.10 per machine with a $35 per machine MDE rebate. Item 9.F. awards AirWatch Enterprise Mobile Device Management software through CDWG for $208,921.50 from the 2014-2015 General Fund on the NJPA bid vehicle, a three-year contract at $66,420 per year for licensing plus $9,661.50 for installation and training, supporting over 5000 new iPads in Fall 2014. Item 11.A. is a 2013/2014 School Year in Review slide show by Kerry Birmingham.

CONSENT AGENDA MINUTES. May 5, 2014 special meeting (called to order 6:00 p.m. by President Philippart; closed session 14-037 on superintendent candidates' assessment review carried 7-0; adjourned 10:35 p.m.). May 6, 2014 board meeting (7:00 p.m., approximately 200 in the audience): Mary Curl of Morse Elementary named Outstanding Support Staff Employee of the Year from nine nominees and announced as the 2014 county-wide Betty Campion award winner, presented by Dr. Vickie Markavitch of Oakland Schools; a State of Michigan Declaration of Special Tribute for Dr. Barbara Fowler's 31 years of service, signed by Senator John Pappageorge and Governor Rick Snyder; Teacher Appreciation Week resolution 14-038 for May 5-9, 2014; consent agenda 14-039 including the March 2014 Treasurer's Report and Air Filters Bid 9775; student reports from Michaela Smith of Athens and Zari Saynganthone of Niles; resolution 14-040 offering the superintendency to Dr. Richard Machesky over finalist Dr. Steve Matthews of Novi Community Schools after a MASB-assisted search with interviews April 21 and April 29 and site visits May 1, carried 7-0; textbook adoptions 14-041 (Glencoe Health 2013 edition, Glencoe Human Sexuality) and 14-042 (The Big Ideas Math Common Core and Precalculus with Limits by Ron Larson); resolution 14-043 supporting the Oakland Intermediate School District budget under Section 624 of the Revised School Code, adopted 6-1 with Edmunds opposed; 14-044 custodial and grounds services with Enviro-Clean for 2014/2015 through 2016/2017 with options for 2017/2018 and 2018/2019; 14-045 continuing Sodexo food service for 2014/15 with renewal options through 2018/19 subject to Michigan Department of Education approval; 14-046 roofing to National Roofing & Sheet Metal Co., Inc. for $1,539,540.00; 14-047 site work to Nagle Paving Company for $1,593,450.00; 14-048 auditorium stage pianos to Evola Music Center for $49,702.00; 14-049 basketball scoreboards to Daktronics, Inc. for $44,420.00; 14-050 track renovations at Athens and Troy High Schools with Nagle Paving Company general construction $288,890.00 and Goddard Coating Company all-weather surface $137,375.00 for a total bid of $426,265.00, all from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund; and second readings adopting revisions to Board Policy C-1402 Smoking (14-051), G-1005 Nondiscrimination (14-052) and J-2012 Anti-Bullying (14-053); adjourned 9:15 p.m. May 15, 2014 special meeting (4:47 p.m., Underwood absent): 14-054 awarding bond Package 1 secure entrances to Construction Solutions, Inc. general trades $1,892,300.00, Miller-Boldt, Inc. mechanical $636,815.00 and Metro Electric Technologies electrical $559,000.00 for a total bid of $3,088,115.00; 14-055 rescinding the April 22, 2014 award of Gumdrop Tech iPad cases to CDWG for $153,000; 14-056 awarding Shield cases to MaxCase for $117,300.00 at $23 per unit against $30 for Gumdrop, a savings of $35,700; and 14-057 designating Karl Schmidt to cast the Troy board's ballot for incumbent George Ehlert at the June 2, 2014 Oakland Schools election under Public Act 419 of 2004 for a six-year term ending June 30, 2020; adjourned 5:13 p.m. May 20, 2014 special meeting (5:00 p.m., Vice President Miletti presiding, attorney John Gierak of Clark Hill present): closed session 14-058 on attorney-client privilege, carried 5-0, adjourned 6:22 p.m. May 20, 2014 board workshop (6:25 p.m. to 10:30 p.m.): Sodexo update, closing the achievement gap including TLLs and Summer Success and Reading Recovery, and One 2 World.
